activity.notes: Thales is securely treated as an early sixth-century BCE Milesian thinker and a foundational figure in Greek natural philosophy. ATLAS uses c.585 BCE only as a representative floruit point anchored in the ancient eclipse tradition; it does not assert that the eclipse prediction itself is historically certain or fabricate a career-long activity interval.

sources.title: Presocratic Philosophy — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.citation_text: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy identifies Thales of Miletus as the earliest Milesian natural philosopher, places him around the beginning of the sixth century BCE, and distinguishes the later eclipse-prediction tradition from secure historical claims.

sources.title: Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book I, Chapter 1: Thales — Perseus Digital Library
sources.citation_text: Diogenes Laertius preserves the ancient tradition of Thales as a Milesian sage and student of nature and gives his floruit as approximately 585 BCE.

spatial_disposition.evidence: Miletus is a securely identified Ionian polis on the western Anatolian coast, and Thales is consistently identified as a Milesian. A static historical display disposition is therefore appropriate; no speculative polity-place function is asserted.
